Subject: Re: Streaming responses stalling during live sessions

Hi Alex — thank you for the logs and the clear timeline. We’re seeing correlated telemetry indicating short-lived token emit lapses from a subset of edge replicas servicing your region (us-west).

Immediate guidance we recommend while we investigate:
- Enable client-side incremental backoff: start with a 200ms reconnect jitter and exponential backoff capping at 3s. See attached sample-client-backoff-config.json.
- Temporarily reduce max_concurrent_streams on your client to 8 for the busiest pods (this reduces pressure on connection multiplexing).
- If you can, enable HTTP/2 keepalive pings every 20s to avoid intermediate proxies closing idle streams.

We’ll run a deeper investigation; looping in Marcus for root-cause analysis and Grace for any capacity adjustments. I’ll update you in 2 hours or sooner.

Best,
Naomi

On Mon, Apr 12, 2027 at 10:28 AM Naomi wrote:
> We’re seeing correlated telemetry indicating short-lived token emit lapses from a subset of edge replicas servicing your region (us-west).

Alex / FinCentric — quick engineering summary and immediate mitigations we’re executing from the Redwood side:
1) We’ve identified a microburst of RPC queueing on two edge replicas connected to the us-west gateway between 09:45–10:20 PDT. Root cause: a transient slowdown in a dependency (gRPC connection churn to the KV cache layer) that increased tail latency for token emission.
2) Actions taken: 1) drained and rotated the two affected replicas; 2) applied an autoscaler patch to avoid rapid scale-down during bursty loads; 3) disabled a new experimental connection pooling heuristic that increased head-of-line blocking.
3) Short-term customer-facing mitigations (recommended):
   - Use the client backoff Naomi attached.
   - Add a 250ms client-side token timeout and retry on short stalls (idempotent requests only).
   - If you rely on streaming for UI latency, enable the fallback to non-streaming chunked responses for flows where partial output is acceptable. Our team can provide sample code.

We’ll continue to monitor; attaching a diagnostic extract (redwood_stream_diagnostics_20270412.log.txt). Marcus

Marcus Lin
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Streaming responses stalling during live sessions — closure and post-incident notes

Hi Alex — quick post-incident summary and next steps. Thanks again for your patience and for testing the mitigations.

What happened (summary):
- Between 09:45–10:20 PDT on 2027-04-12 we observed elevated token emit tail latency affecting a subset of edge replicas in us-west. The immediate trigger was gRPC connection churn to the KV cache under a microburst load pattern, which transiently increased head-of-line blocking for streaming token emission.

What we did (actions completed):
- Rotated the two impacted replicas and disabled the experimental pooling heuristic.
- Applied an autoscaler tuning change to smooth scale-down behavior during bursty traffic.
- Added a temporary routing preference to favor warmed replicas for FinCentric traffic while we monitored stability.

Customer impact & credits:
- We measured ~28 minutes of elevated latency that affected FinCentric’s requests. We will apply a one-off service credit equal to 5% of the billed usage during the affected window; your Redwoods account manager will follow up with a formal reconciliation and the credit note.

Follow-up items (owners & ETA):
- Engineering (Marcus): finalize a fix to the connection pooling heuristic and submit change by 2027-04-21.
- SRE (Grace): roll out improved canary checks for KV cache latency by 2027-04-20.
- Account (Naomi): deliver chunked-response fallback sample code and a short integration guide by 2027-04-16.

Attachments: postmortem-notes-20270414.pdf (incident timeline + telemetry graphs), sample-client-backoff-config.json.

If you’d like a short call to review the postmortem graphs and the code sample, I can schedule 30 minutes tomorrow afternoon.
